name: Mint a runner key
description: Admin only. Mints the credential a runner presents at POST /v1/runner/token, and returns it EXACTLY ONCE: the table stores sha256 of it, so this response is the only place the key material ever exists outside the operator's hands. That is the whole reason for the shape -- reading runner_keys does not let anyone start a runner, and the blast radius of a leaked database dump does not include the fleet. The prefix is minted separately rather than cut off the key with substring arithmetic, so the stored display string and the key cannot disagree. A key is a row and not a column on users, which is what makes rotation a second key rather than a gap: hold two, retire one.

with.name: Admins only
with.description: The role is read off the live session rather than off a claim in the cookie, so revoking a session or demoting a user takes effect on the next request.

tasks.name: Parse payload
tasks.description: AFTER the admin check, not before it: there is no reason to parse a body sent by someone who is not allowed to be here, and the three tasks above answer that with one read.

with.name: A key is named
with.description: Checked here rather than left to the CHECK constraint, because a constraint violation inside db_write is a 500 and this is a caller's omission.

tasks.name: Mint the key
tasks.description: Two mappings, not one: a params element folds {"var": ...} and nothing else, so both halves must exist in temp_data before the insert can name them. `random bytes 32` is 256 bits of key material; the prefix is 8 hex characters that identify the key in a list and unlock nothing.

tasks.name: Hash the key
tasks.description: sha256, not password_hash: the token exchange has to FIND the row from the key alone, and a deterministic digest makes that one indexed probe. A salted hash would force a scan and a verify per row, which is the wrong trade for 256 bits of machine-generated randomness.

with.name: The session went away
with.description: The preamble passed, so the only thing that can have emptied this insert is the session being revoked or the role dropped between the two statements. The JOIN is inside the INSERT for exactly that window.

tasks.name: Read the key back
tasks.description: Keyed on key_hash, which is UNIQUE: db_write answers only rows_affected, so the created row is read back, and a read-back needs a unique predicate.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('id', k.id, 'label', k.label, 'key_prefix', k.key_prefix, 'created_at', k.created_at) AS body FROM runner_keys k WHERE k.key_hash = ($1)::text

logic.note: Copy this key now. It is stored as a hash and cannot be shown again; if it is lost, revoke it and mint another.
